subject: Accelerated usage bridge + transient rate lock for renewal
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Rateel Shah <rateel@clearpath.com>
Cc: procure@clearpath.com
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Accelerated usage bridge + transient rate lock for renewal

Hi Rateel —

Thanks again for the call last week. Based on the usage profile you shared and the uptick you expect across search and summarization queries, we put together a short bridge proposal to protect ClearPath from step-up price exposure while you scale through Q4. The idea is to give you a time-limited rate lock on your current effective price for an accelerated-usage tranche, plus a modest one-time credit to offset immediate invoice timing concerns while you finalize your long-term commit.

High-level:
- Term: 6-month bridge starting Oct 1 → transient rate lock at current effective price for the tranche.
- Bridge tranche: +40% of current committed vCPU/GPU hours for the six months (billed as usage).
- One-time usage credit: $45,000 billed as a debit on first renewal invoice (applies only if you convert to a 12-month commit by Feb 1).
- True-up and rollover: any usage beyond the bridge that becomes persistent is eligible to roll into a standard commit with pro-rated credit back to ClearPath.

Attached is a short one-pager and the Q3 usage export that informed the sizing.

If that structure sounds reasonable I can loop in Marissa and Ben for the final pricing and legal checklist and share a DocuSign when you’re ready. Would you prefer a canary start (tiered ramp) or full tranche activation on Oct 1?

—David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Rateel Shah <rateel@clearpath.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@clearpath.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Accelerated usage bridge + transient rate lock for renewal

David —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the one-pager. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

1) Invoice timing: we close books on the 25th of the month. Any credits that post after our close will push recognition to next quarter; would it be possible to structure the $45k as an invoice-level credit applied to the Oct invoice (so it hits our Q4)?

2) Pricing runway: we want the rate lock to be effective for any traffic that maps to our product tier, not per-model. Can you confirm that the lock covers the current mix of models we use (gpt-like open variants + one custom quantized variant)?

3) Procurement:+legal redlines — our procurement team prefers a short amendment rather than a full new SOW; they asked for an outline of the minimal contract language changes you need. I’ve included procure@clearpath.com on the thread.

We’d prefer a canary ramp (20% → 60% → full) over two weeks if that keeps ops stable.

—Rateel
Rateel Shah
Head of Platform
ClearPath Labs
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ClearPath — bridge proposal (procurement asks)

FYI — Rateel pushed back on credit timing and wants the rate lock to cover model mix. Procurement wants an amendment. Key asks:
- Can we make the $45k an invoice credit applied to Oct invoice (so it posts in Q4) rather than debit on renewal?
- Confirm that rate lock applies to model family (not single model) and to their current quantized variant. Ops: is the canary ramp OK? They want a 2-week ramp.

Propose we offer: invoice credit applied Oct invoice conditional on conversion to 12-month commit by Feb 1 (so credit is contingent but applied upfront), and explicit language that rate lock applies to this customer’s active model set (documented in schedule). I’ll let you price the concession.

Thanks — David
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ClearPath — bridge proposal (procurement asks)

Agree with David’s framing. Suggested commercial adjustments:

- One-time invoice credit: $45,000 applied to Oct invoice (we will include a conditional clawback clause: if customer does not sign a 12-month commit by Feb 1, the credit converts to a standard invoice and is payable in the next billing cycle).
- Transient rate lock scope: covers the customer’s declared model mix (three model families listed in Schedule A) and any model variants that are byte-equivalent; excludes materially different model classes (e.g., new Llama-4 style architectures). We’ll capture the model list in the amendment to avoid ambiguity.
- Bridge tranche pricing: apply existing effective unit price up to the bridge limit; above that, usage billed at standard pay-as-you-go.
- Ramp: support the 2-week canary (20% → 60% → 100%) with ops playbook. Ops will require a short on-call window for the first 72 hours of each ramp step.

Ben — can you confirm the $45k math and whether we want to encode a 1.5% service fee on rolled-over commit conversions (to account for quick provisioning overhead)? If not, I’ll leave it out.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Deals
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Rateel Shah <rateel@clearpath.com>, procure@clearpath.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Accelerated usage bridge + transient rate lock for renewal — agreed next steps

Rateel / ClearPath team —

Thanks for the quick turn. We’ve agreed internally and can do the following:

1) Commercial summary (short):
   - 6-month bridge starting Oct 1 with a transient rate lock applied to the declared model families in Schedule A.
   - Bridge tranche = +40% of current committed compute capacity for 6 months, billed as usage at your current effective unit rate up to the tranche cap.
   - $45,000 invoice credit to be applied to the Oct invoice. The credit will be conditional: if ClearPath executes a 12-month commit by Feb 1, the credit remains; otherwise it will be invoiced back in the next cycle.
   - Canary ramp: 20% → 60% → 100% over two weeks; Redwood Ops will monitor and provide a 72-hour on-call for each step.

2) Contract path: we will issue an amendment (not a full SOW). The amendment will contain: schedule listing model families (Schedule A), the credit clause with the conditional clawback, and the ramp/ops commitments. Legal will keep changes minimal.

3) Next actions / timeline:
   - I’ll share the amendment + a clean DocuSign by EOD Thursday. (Link: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/ABC-987654)
   - Procurement: if you want us to use your amendment template, we can accept redlines limited to the three items above; please highlight required changes in the template.
   - Ops: confirm canary window and provide the list of contact names for the three ramp days.

Attachments: CPL_Renewal_Bridge_v1.pdf (one-pager), usage_report_Q3.csv

If that aligns, we’ll route DocuSign and Ops playbook today.

Best —
David Kim
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
